$comment: Per-machine configuration. **It follows the person** — moving to another
directory to do work should not change your keys.
The file that takes effect is ~/.tudouni/config.json; the copy with the same
name in the repository is only the thing that gets copied.
**There is exactly one source of configuration**: this file. No environment
variables, no .env. To change something, change this file.
providers: **the key is the route name**, and the order is the order of the
/model list — that is, you decide which one is the default by ordering them:
the first route that has a key is the default route. A route gives three things:
base_url    where requests go
api_key     the key goes right here (there is no second way to write it)
models      what is on that route; omit it and the route cannot be selected
If you do not know context_window, delete the whole line: then the interface
reports usage without a percentage. A wrong percentage is worse than none —
it gets treated as true.
api_style: which wire protocol this endpoint speaks. Omit the line and it is
worked out from base_url, which is right for almost every route. Write it only
to override that:
openai      POST base_url/chat/completions   (the default)
anthropic   POST base_url/v1/messages        (Claude, and the
Anthropic-compatible endpoints of MiniMax, Qwen, ...)
responses   POST base_url/v1/responses
The inference reads the end of base_url, so ending it in /messages,
/v1/messages or /anthropic is enough. Nothing else is adjusted: if the
endpoint is reached at /v1/messages, base_url must not already end in /v1.
headers: extra request headers, sent on every request to that route. Some
vendors require their own client identification — a custom User-Agent or a
session header — and this is the only way to say so. Values are strings.
reasoning_effort / effort_levels: the thinking levels. `reasoning_effort` on a
model is the level that model starts on; `effort_levels` is which levels it
accepts, and it is what /effort offers and enforces. Put effort_levels on the
route to cover all its models, or on one model to override that.
Leave both out and /effort offers the whole vocabulary — minimal, low, medium,
high, xhigh, max — and a level the model does not take comes back as an error
from the endpoint. That is the deliberate default: listing too much costs one
visible error, while listing too little hides a level that works, and nobody
reports a level they cannot see. Declare effort_levels when you know better;
the values are never rewritten, so what you pick is what goes on the wire.
`none` is not a level: it means thinking off, which is /thinking, not /effort.
web: the keys for web search. Leave them out and web_search is not registered
(fetch_web is unaffected; a missing key there is not an error).
image_generation: the route that draws pictures. Leave it out and generate_image
is not registered — the capability is simply not there, and nothing else changes.
provider: the chat route to inherit the key and the endpoint from, so one key
is written once. The routes are the names under `providers`.
model:    the image model (gpt-image-1 and the like). It is **never** inherited:
the chat route's model is a different model.
api_style: which wire protocol this endpoint speaks. Only one is implemented:
openai-images   POST base_url/images/generations
base_url / api_key / headers: write them here to override what was inherited.
A generation endpoint is often not the chat endpoint — some gateways serve
only one of the two — so an inherited base_url may answer 404 for
/images/generations. The error message names the URL that was used.
The picture lands in the workspace as a real file (out/poster.png): it can be
shown with ![](path), declared with present, and opened again later.

headers-example.$comment: A route that needs its own client identification. The api_key carries the credential; these ride along with it, and neither is invented from a provider name.

image_generation.$comment: Uncomment and fill in to enable generate_image. Delete the whole section to turn it off.
